newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's coffee shortfall squeezing Federation.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's coffee shortfall squeezing Federation.

text.p: The head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said it was having "enormous difficulties" meeting its export commitments because of unusally tight supply.
"There's very little coffee in Colombia. The federation is having enormous difficulties meeting its commitments," Jorge Cardenas told reporters after a weekly policy meeting.

"Unfortunately the (1996/97) crop, as of the last day of April, stood at 10.2 million (60-kg) bags compared to 14.3 a year ago," Cardenas added, explaining why the federation had been forced to draw on 1.2 million 60-kilo bags of coffee in its stocks to help meet export commitments since October.
"There's been a delay in shipments for April," Cardenas added, openly acknowledging that the country had fallen behind on its export schedules.

He said the federation and private exporters had planned to ship a combined total of 900,000 60-kg bags of coffee in April, but this may have been unrealistic given average shipments of no more than 800,000 bags over the past few months.

Cardenas said he hoped Colombia's supply problems would ease by October. But in the meantime, he said the country's coffee industry was passing through an "extremely difficult" time in which the federation was basically fighting for every available bag of coffee with private exporters.
